items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: this was before Frank Shiffman.] Frank Shiffman seems to have been forever there, but this was another guy that had this, the theater at the time.

ctx.x: How far back does that go?

Oh, that goes back into the '20s. But it's quite an old theater. It's been there for many, many years. Our first outing there at the Apollo was in 1934, and it came about more or less in an accidental way. Fletcher Henderson had broken up his band and Benny Carter had signed a contract to appear at the Apollo and he thought he was going to get -- believe it or not, there was a shortage, when I say competent black musicians, I mean guys that could read, you know. There was a lot of guys around that could play, but…

thing with the xylophones and oh, he broke it up too, he really did. Of course you know Red was quite a performer before he became strictly a jazz player. I mean he was quite a showman. Did you ever see him chop that xylophone up? Well, he used to hit the xylophone. The climax to the whole thing is all the notes in the xylophone are -- he had a bunch of loose ones there, and they're flying all over the stage. It was sort of a comedy type thing.
